consensus_summary: Dominant Christian symbolic reading of kaph is God’s intimate protective care, permanent remembrance, and secure holding of His people (chiefly Isa 49:16 engraving on the palms), frequently linked to prayer/supplication by open palms, moral purity of deeds (‘clean hands’), and broader hand imagery of agency/power; some responses note no single settled code beyond contextual hand symbolism.
book_summary: Kaph is the open hand laid open—to cover, carry, or offer—distinct from yad (hand of power); illustrated by the palm covering Moses, Zion graven on the palms, the virtuous woman stretching out to the poor, and prayer spread toward heaven (Isa 62:3 holds both terms).
consensus_core_identification: Divine protective care/remembrance via the palms (Isa 49:16), with open-palm prayer and agency as common extensions
book_core_identification: The open hand (kaph) specifically for covering, carrying, and offering, lexically opposed to yad as power
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts kaph to the open-hand functions of cover/carry/offer and sharply separates it from yad-power, whereas consensus treats care/remembrance as primary but freely mixes kaph with general hand (yad/right-hand) agency, purity, and power imagery without that lexical boundary.
rationale: Both center on the same Isa 49:16 / covering / prayer cluster; the book does not replace the referent but narrows and re-precision it to ‘open hand for cover-carry-offer’ while excluding or reclassifying pure power/agency and purity-of-deeds senses that consensus admits under kaph. Differences are boundary and emphasis, not contradictory cores.
strongest_objection: Consensus (esp. A/B/D) treats remembrance/care as the settled primary symbol and power/purity as ordinary extensions; the book’s lexical open-vs-power refinement and inclusion of Prov 31 generosity could be viewed as selective rather than the dominant traditional reading.
